question: Should existing GitHub-backed over-limit display names be grandfathered like hosted rows, or may sync rewrite them to capped names on the next run?
rationale: This is stored catalog compatibility and product-policy behavior; automation should not choose whether already-published source-backed names may change during upgrade.

options.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed names
options.body: Preserve matched existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names unless the source changes under an approved policy, and add a regression test for that upgrade path.

options.title: Approve rename-on-sync
options.body: Allow next-sync rewrites intentionally, but document the upgrade behavior and require proof that the rewrite is expected and bounded.

options.title: Pause until policy is set
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define the display-name maximum and legacy behavior across hosted and GitHub-backed sources.

recommendation.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed names
recommendation.body: Preserve matched existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names unless the source changes under an approved policy, and add a regression test for that upgrade path.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick owns the recent central publish and GitHub-source sync code where this compatibility policy lands.
